title: Gates Foundation and OpenAI — AI-for-health systems (Horizon1000), Rwanda, 2026
description: "The pilot initiative, known as Horizon1000, will combine $50 million in funding, technology, and technical support to help countries apply AI tools that strengthen primary healthcare delivery." "Implementation will begin in Rwanda, with plans to scale the programme to 1,000 primary healthcare clinics and surrounding communities across multiple countries by 2028." The programme targets Sub-Saharan Africa's estimated health-workforce shortage of 5.6 million.

title: Paradigm Tower Ventures \u2014 Investment (Shared Telecom Infrastructure)
description: BII committed $44.4M to Paradigm Infrastructure in September 2025, established in 2019 to pursue opportunities to develop shared telecoms tower infrastructure across Sub-Saharan Africa. Paradigm operates and leases tower sites to mobile network operators, enabling expanded network coverage especially in underserved rural areas. The investment directly supports mobile broadband connectivity and digital inclusion across multiple SSA markets.

However, a large proportion of the population still lacks direct access to these resources and services. title: Scaling DPI in Rwanda and launching an African Centre for DPI
description: To accelerate economic inclusion and reduce poverty by supporting Rwanda's efforts to build safe and inclusive digital public infrastructure, including interoperable payments, identity, and data sharing systems.

title: Strengthening Rwanda Industrial Standardisation ICT Capacity (SISIC) Project
description: KOICA grant ($8M, 2024-2028) with Rwanda Standards Board (RSB) to boost technology in advancing Rwanda's industrial standardisation. Empowers SMEs across key sectors, enhancing competitiveness through ICT tools for standards compliance.

title: Rwanda Digital Transformation (First AFD Sovereign Digital Loan to Rwanda)
description: First AFD sovereign digital transformation loan to Rwanda. Supports expansion of digital public services, e-government infrastructure, and digital economy. Rwanda is advancing Irembo (national e-service platform) and digital ID systems.

title: Project for Introduction of Intelligent Transport System (ITS) in Kigali City
description: JICA grant aid for deployment of intelligent transport system at 20 intersections in Kigali City. Includes traffic control equipment (traffic lights and traffic control consoles), road-surface markings, detailed design and supervision, and technical assistance for facility management including development of manuals, operation of traffic control and signal control systems, and analysis of traffic data. Grant agreement signed October 5, 2023.

title: Rwanda Social Protection Transformation Project \u2014 Digital Payment Systems Component
description: Components 3 and 4 (combined ~$13.5M of $100M total) of the Rwanda Social Protection Transformation Project support nationwide digital payment systems for VUP social transfers via mobile money (MTN/Airtel), SACCO digitization, dynamic social registry, and digital beneficiary management systems.

title: Kigali Innovation City (KIC) Technopark PPP Development
description: Africa50 is co-developer and equity co-sponsor of Kigali Innovation City (KIC), a 60-hectare mixed-use, masterplanned innovation city in Kigali, Rwanda, developed under a public-private partnership with the Rwanda Development Board (RDB). The project includes Grade A offices, a technology incubator, retail, hospitality, residential and four planned universities. Africa50 IC approval December 2022; groundbreaking September 2024. Total project value estimated USD 300 million–USD 2 billion at full build-out. Expected to generate USD 150 million in annual ICT exports and attract USD 300 million in FDI.
recipient_organisation: Kigali Innovation City Company / Rwanda Development Board

title: Smart Education Project
description: CHEXIM concessional loan for a Smart Education Project in Rwanda, deploying digital technology infrastructure to support education delivery. Likely includes ICT equipment, connectivity, and digital learning platforms for educational institutions.
recipient_organisation: Government of Rwanda / Ministry of Education

title: Rwanda National Digital Payment System (R-NDPS) L1P aligned upgrade
description: to upgrade Rwanda’s existing national switch using Mojaloop open-source technology to support Rwanda’s goal of a Level One principles aligned payment system in accordance with Rwanda’s National Digital Payment System (RNDPS) blueprint.

title: Rwanda Digital and Innovation Promotion Project
description: JICA technical cooperation project 2022-2026 to establish Rwanda as leading ICT hub in Africa through market creation and innovation model development. Four outputs: entrepreneur supply systems, innovation ecosystem via public-private partnerships, integrated ICT initiative capacity, and Rwanda model for market expansion. Builds on predecessor ICT Innovation Ecosystem Strengthening Project (2017-2022).

title: Project for Enhancing Digital Literacy through the Digital Ambassador Program (DAP)
description: KOICA grant ($4.5M, 2022-2026) implemented with Rwanda Information Society Authority (RISA). Deployed 1,000 Digital Ambassadors and 30 supervisors nationwide to train 1,567,034 citizens in basic digital skills and access to e-government services. Established 5 Service Access Points.

title: CMU-Africa: Center for Inclusive Digital Transformation of Africa
description: MCF $275.7M partnership with Carnegie Mellon University and Government of Rwanda to expand engineering, AI and technology education at CMU-Africa in Kigali. Includes $175M endowment for CMU-Africa and $100.7M for the new Center for the Inclusive Digital Transformation of Africa (Upanzi Network). Target: 10,000 young Africans in digital skills and digital transformation careers.

title: Airtel Mobile Money Rwanda \u2013 Digital Financial Services Guarantee
description: MIGA political risk guarantee covering The Rise Fund II Aurora S.à r.l. (TPG private equity) equity investment in Airtel Mobile Commerce B.V.'s subsidiary providing Airtel Money digital financial services in Rwanda. Services include mobile wallet (cash-in/cash-out), airtime recharging, bill payments, merchant payments; with international transfers, savings and microloans in some markets. Risks: war and civil disturbance, expropriation, transfer restriction and inconvertibility for up to 5 years.

title: Digital Acceleration Project
description: Accelerates Rwanda's digital economy through enhanced broadband connectivity, digital financial services, digital government platforms, and digital skills. Part of DE4A initiative.

title: Rwanda Digital Acceleration Project (Digital Investment for Recovery, Resilience and Connectivity)
description: A whole-of-government digital acceleration initiative to support Rwanda's short-run and long-term recovery from the pandemic and resilience to future pandemics by increasing access to broadband and selected digital public services, and strengthening the digital innovation ecosystem. Four components: (1) Digital Access and Inclusion USD60.5M — last-mile connectivity, affordable smart devices, digital literacy/skills, broadband market development; (2) Digital Public Service Delivery USD100M — national ID system strengthening, e-services, cybersecurity, data protection, government data management; (3) Digital Innovation and Entrepreneurship USD29.5M — early-stage finance for digital start-ups, bootcamp programmes for advanced digital skills; (4) Project Management USD10M. AIIB's first digital investment in Sub-Saharan Africa.
recipient_organisation: Rwanda Information Society Authority (RISA); Development Bank of Rwanda (BRD); Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning, Rwanda

description: KOICA grant ($6M, 2018-2020) to Rwanda Revenue Authority to develop full-scale EBM Version 2 system and Taxpayer Relationship Management System. Built on pilot Phase 1 EBM 2017 results. Enhanced VAT compliance and digital tax administration across Rwanda.

title: The ICT Innovation Ecosystem Strengthening Project (Rwanda)
description: JICA technical cooperation project to strengthen Rwanda's ICT innovation ecosystem. Duration October 2017 - March 2022 (66 months). Established 250STARTUPS early-incubation mechanism, three innovation hubs in secondary cities, supported 58 startups, matched 17 Rwandan-Japanese company MOUs/LOIs, supported 10 proof-of-concept projects. Aimed to position Rwanda as Africa's leading ICT hub.

title: Capacity Development for ICT in Education (CADIE) in Rwanda
description: KOICA grant (2017-2024, $7.3M) to Rwanda Education Board under MINEDUC. Established 69 ICT smart classrooms (Centres of Excellence) in secondary schools, trained ~30,000 teachers in ICT integration. Developed ICT competency curriculum and 129 master trainers.
